tools.name: chirpie_upload_media
tools.description: Upload an image or a video and get back the id a post can attach. Give it either a public `url` for Chirpie to fetch, or `data`, the file's bytes as base64. The file type is read from the file's own first bytes, never from its name or a declared type, so a mislabelled file is refused rather than published. The id is valid for 7 days; attach it with `media: [{ id, alt }]` on chirpie_post, chirpie_thread or chirpie_update_post. A post keeps its own copy of the bytes, so it is unaffected when the id expires. Uploads are limited to 3 MB of file when sent as `data`, which bounds the request rather than the post; attach a larger file with media_urls instead, which has no such limit.

url.description: A public image or video URL for Chirpie to fetch and store.

data.description: The file's bytes, base64 encoded. Use this or url, not both.

filename.description: A name to show in the dashboard. Never used to decide the file type.

idempotency_key.description: A key of your own making that makes retrying this call safe. The same key with the same request replays the first answer for 24 hours instead of sending it again; the same key with a different request is refused with 422 idempotency_key_reused, and a retry that arrives while the first is still running is refused with 409 idempotency_in_progress; a retry after the first has finished collects the replay.

tools.name: chirpie_post
tools.description: Create a post on X/Twitter, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Threads, Mastodon, Instagram, Facebook, or Telegram with optional media. Posts immediately or at a scheduled time. Publish to several accounts at once by naming account_ids instead of account_id, and give one of them its own text or media with account_configurations. Note: Instagram REQUIRES media. X posts whose text contains a link are billed at $0.25 each on paid plans and are rejected on the Free plan (x_link_posts_require_paid_plan); X accounts connected with your own X API keys are exempt. A spent monthly post or scheduled-post quota answers 429 usage_limit_exceeded, which waiting does not clear; the separate per-minute burst limit on the API key answers 429 rate_limited and does clear. Set draft: true to save the post without sending it: nothing reaches the platform, nothing counts against the monthly quota, the text may even be empty, and the answer carries a `warnings` array saying per account what would go wrong if it were sent as it stands. chirpie_update_post edits a draft and promotes it with schedule_at or publish: true.

account_id.description: Account ID to post from (X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Threads, Mastodon, Instagram, Facebook, or Telegram). Use this or account_ids, not both.

account_ids.description: Account IDs to publish the same post to, 1 to 25 of them, each named once. Naming this instead of account_id answers with a group_id and one result per account, in the order given, each with its own `success`: an account whose platform refused is reported there while the others stay published. Anything that fails the request as a whole (a character limit, a media rule, a spent quota) publishes nothing.

account_configurations.description: Per-account overrides, keyed by account ID. Every key must also be in account_ids. An account with no entry publishes the shared text and media. Media never merges: an account naming any media field replaces the shared media outright. Use one media spelling at a time.

text.description: Text for this account only, instead of the shared text.

media.description: Media for this account only, replacing the shared media. An empty array publishes this account with no media.

id.description: The id chirpie_upload_media returned. Valid for 7 days.

url.description: A public image or video URL for Chirpie to fetch.

alt.description: A description of the item, for people using a screen reader.

media_ids.description: Ids from chirpie_upload_media, for this account only.

media_urls.description: Public image or video URLs for this account only.

first_comment.description: A first comment for this account only, instead of the shared one. An empty string publishes this account with no first comment at all, which is how a fan-out sends one to the accounts that take a first comment while an account that does not still publishes the post. Leave it out and the account inherits the shared one.

configuration.description: Publishing options for this account only, instead of the shared ones. The whole block is replaced rather than merged, so an account publishing as a reel while the rest go to the feed carries its own instagram block.

instagram.description: How an Instagram account publishes this post. A story carries no caption (send empty text), no first comment and no collaborators. A reel takes one video, collaborators, user tags, a cover, share_to_feed and trial_reel.

placement.description: Where the post goes: feed (the default) takes up to 10 images, story takes exactly one image or video, reel takes exactly one video and no images.

collaborators.description: Up to 3 Instagram usernames to invite as co-authors, without the @. The post appears on a collaborator's profile once they accept the invitation, which happens on Instagram. Feed posts and reels only.

user_tags.description: The people to tag. A feed post needs both x and y on every tag, a story may carry both or neither, and a reel takes the username on its own, because Instagram reads coordinates only on images and stories. Tags belong to one image, so a carousel carrying them is refused.

x.description: Distance from the left edge, 0 to 1.

y.description: Distance from the top edge, 0 to 1.

cover.description: The id of an uploaded image to use as a reel's cover. Use this or video_cover_timestamp_ms, never both: Instagram reads the image and ignores the timestamp, so sending both would drop one of the two things you asked for.

video_cover_timestamp_ms.description: A frame of the reel itself to use as its cover, in milliseconds.

share_to_feed.description: Whether a reel also appears on the profile grid.

trial_reel.description: Publish as a trial reel, shown to people who do not follow the account first. Reels only.

graduation.description: How the reel reaches the account's followers: 'manual' waits for the customer to release it, 'performance' releases it once Instagram decides it is doing well.

facebook.description: How a Facebook Page publishes this post.

placement.description: Where the post goes on the Page: feed (the default), or story, which takes exactly one image or video, no text and no first comment.

link.description: A URL to attach to a feed post, shown as a link preview. Feed posts only.

An entry takes either `id`, from chirpie_upload_media, or `url`, a public link Chirpie fetches. `alt` describes the item for people using a screen reader and is carried to X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Instagram and Facebook. Use this or media_urls, not both. Images per post: X 4, Bluesky 4 (977 KB each), LinkedIn 4 (JPEG, PNG, GIF up to 8 MB), Threads 1, Mastodon 4, Instagram 10 (carousel), Facebook 10, Telegram 10. Video: X, Mastodon and Telegram only, one per post and never alongside images. Instagram REQUIRES at least 1 image. Anything a platform cannot take is refused with 400 unsupported_media, never dropped.

media_urls.description: Public image or video URLs, for a post that needs no alt text. Same per-platform rules as `media`.

first_comment.description: A comment to publish under the post the moment it goes out, the "link in the first comment" pattern. It counts as one post against the monthly quota, like a reply, and on X a first comment containing a link carries the same $0.25 surcharge a link post does and is rejected on the Free plan. It never fails the post: if it cannot be posted the post is still published and the answer carries first_comment with status "failed" and a reason, which chirpie_retry_first_comment sends again.

One block serves every account of that platform; give one account its own with an account_configurations entry.

tools.name: chirpie_thread
tools.description: Create a thread (multiple posts) on X/Twitter, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Threads, Mastodon, Instagram, Facebook, or Telegram. Publish to several accounts at once by naming account_ids instead of account_id, and give one of them a thread of its own with account_configurations. X, Bluesky, Threads, Mastodon, and Telegram support native reply threading. Others degrade gracefully to standalone posts. A THREAD IS ATOMIC: if any part fails, every part already published is deleted from the platform and the whole thread's quota is refunded, and the error's `thread_rollback` says what was rolled back. Two codes tell you whether a retry is safe: `upstream_error` means nothing of the thread is on the platform, so repeating the request is safe, while `thread_rollback_incomplete` means the posts named in `thread_rollback.still_live` are still up with their ids and URLs, and repeating the request would publish them twice. On an Instagram account connected by signing in with Instagram, where Chirpie cannot delete a published post, a failed thread always reports its published parts as still live. On X, each post in the thread whose text contains a link is billed at $0.25 on paid plans; on the Free plan such threads are rejected (x_link_posts_require_paid_plan). X accounts connected with your own X API keys are exempt. A thread that would cross the monthly post or scheduled-post quota answers 429 usage_limit_exceeded and publishes nothing; the per-minute burst limit on the API key answers 429 rate_limited. Set draft: true to save the thread without sending it: nothing reaches the platform, nothing counts against the quota, a draft thread may still be a single part long, and the answer carries a `warnings` array. chirpie_update_post on any of its parts promotes it, and the whole thread goes together.

account_ids.description: Account IDs to publish the same thread to, 1 to 25 of them, each named once. Naming this instead of account_id answers with a group_id and one result per account, in the order given, each with its own `success`: an account whose platform refused is reported there while the others stay published.

tools.name: chirpie_list_posts
tools.description: List recent posts. Filter by status or account. Every post carries `error_message` and `retry_count`: on a failed post the platform's own refusal and how many attempts it took before Chirpie gave up, and on a deleted one the reason Chirpie cancelled it (`account_disconnected`, `account_deactivated`, or `connection_lost` when the platform stopped accepting the account's credential). `platform_post_url` is the public permalink once published. A post the user deleted stays in the listing with status 'deleted' and no cancel reason: Chirpie never removes a post's history. Posts the user hid with chirpie_hide_post are left out unless include_hidden is true, and `hidden` on each post says which those are.

status.description: Filter: draft, scheduled, publishing, published, failed, deleted. With no filter the listing is what has been sent, queued or tried, so drafts are left out; ask for them with status 'draft'.

group_id.description: Only the posts of one fan-out, from the group_id a multi-account chirpie_post or chirpie_thread returned. Every post also carries its own group_id, or null when it went to a single account.

include_hidden.description: Include posts the user hid with chirpie_hide_post. Off by default on every filter, because hiding is the user saying they do not want to see it.

tools.name: chirpie_get_post
tools.description: Get a single post by ID. `platform_post_url` is its public link on the platform; a Threads or Instagram post published without one has it asked for again here. A post that did not go out explains itself in `error_message` and `retry_count`; when the reason is `connection_lost` the account needs reconnecting before anything else will publish, and chirpie_list_accounts says which one.

tools.name: chirpie_update_post
tools.description: Edit a post that has not published yet, or finish a draft. Only a post still waiting to publish can be edited; one that is publishing, published, failed or deleted is refused with 409 post_not_editable. Leaving schedule_at out keeps the time a queued post already has, so editing a queued post never publishes it and never turns it into an immediate one, and costs nothing, since it spent its quota when it was created. Rescheduling a post that belongs to a thread moves every part of that thread, and the response lists them in rescheduled_post_ids. A draft is different: it is held to far less, so an edit that leaves it too long or with no text at all is saved and answers with a `warnings` array instead of an error. Promoting a draft is the one thing this call does publish: schedule_at queues it, publish: true sends it now, both run every rule a create runs and spend the quota the draft never spent, and the answer carries the new post plus promoted_from_draft_id. draft: true alongside schedule_at changes only the time the draft remembers.

text.description: Replacement text. The same per-platform character limits apply as when creating a post.

media.description: Replacement media, following the same per-platform rules as creating a post. Pass an empty array to remove the media.

id.description: The id chirpie_upload_media returned. Valid for 7 days.

url.description: A public image or video URL for Chirpie to fetch.

alt.description: A description of the item, for people using a screen reader.

media_urls.description: Replacement public image or video URLs, for a post that needs no alt text. Pass an empty array to remove the media.

first_comment.description: A new first comment, or an empty string to remove the one the post carries. This is also how a first comment is added to a post that never had one, as long as it has not published yet. On a thread it belongs to the thread, so it applies whichever part you addressed.

configuration.description: New publishing options, or an empty object to put the post back to a plain feed post. Leaving it out keeps the options the post already carries, and sending a block replaces them outright rather than merging into them. The same rules a create runs apply, so a placement the post's media or text does not suit is refused with 400 configuration_unsupported.

schedule_at.description: New ISO 8601 publish time, in the future. Either an absolute instant carrying a timezone, such as '2027-04-01T14:00:00Z', or a local time with no offset, such as '2027-04-01T09:30:00', which is read in the timezone parameter or the one saved on the account. draft.description: Keep this a draft, whatever else changes. Only meaningful on a post that is already a draft, where it is the difference between remembering a new time and queueing the post for it.

publish.description: Publish this draft now. Only valid on a draft, and never together with schedule_at. The draft is checked in full and charged as a post, then sent.

tools.name: chirpie_delete_post
tools.description: Delete a post. If it was already published, the platform is told first, and the post is reported deleted only once the platform confirms it is gone; if the platform refuses or is unavailable the call fails with upstream_error and nothing changes, so the same request can simply be retried. If it has not gone out yet, nothing reaches a platform at all: a queued post is cancelled and its quota returned (cancelled_ids), while a draft is simply marked deleted (deleted_ids) and nothing is returned, because a draft never counted against any quota. Deleting a draft returns no quota. A published TikTok post, a Facebook Page story, and any published post on an Instagram account connected by signing in with Instagram rather than through a Facebook Page cannot be deleted through the platform's API, so each is refused with delete_unsupported rather than reported deleted and stays published; it can be deleted in the platform's own app, and chirpie_hide_post keeps it out of the Chirpie listings. THE POST IS NEVER REMOVED FROM CHIRPIE: it keeps its id and its history with status 'deleted', so chirpie_get_post still returns it. Deleting any post of a scheduled thread cancels the whole thread: a thread is published as a unit, so it is cancelled as one. Deleting a published post reaches the platform and cannot be undone; chirpie_hide_post is the reversible alternative, which changes only what Chirpie shows.

tools.name: chirpie_retry_first_comment
tools.description: Post a first comment that failed, again. A first comment never fails its post, so a published post can be carrying first_comment with status "failed" and a reason; this re-sends the text the post already holds. That text cannot be changed once the post is out, because chirpie_update_post refuses a published post with 409 post_not_editable, so set it while the post is still a draft or still queued. A first comment is a post on the platform, so a retry that works costs one post from the monthly quota, exactly as the first attempt would have. Refusals: 404 first_comment_not_found when the post has none, 409 first_comment_not_retryable when it is already posted or the post has not published, and the platform's own refusal when the retry failed too.

id.description: The post whose first comment to retry. For a thread, the last part, which is the one that carries it.

idempotency_key.description: A key of your own making that makes retrying this call safe. The same key with the same request replays the first answer for 24 hours instead of sending it again; the same key with a different request is refused with 422 idempotency_key_reused, and a retry that arrives while the first is still running is refused with 409 idempotency_in_progress; a retry after the first has finished collects the replay.

tools.name: chirpie_hide_post
tools.description: Hide a post from the user's Chirpie listings. NOTHING REACHES THE PLATFORM: the post stays exactly as it is, keeps its analytics and its comments, and chirpie_unhide_post puts it back. Nothing is charged and no quota moves. Hiding changes only what Chirpie shows; chirpie_delete_post is what takes a post down from the platform. A hidden post is left out of chirpie_list_posts unless include_hidden is true, and is always readable by id with chirpie_get_post. HIDING A QUEUED POST DOES NOT STOP IT PUBLISHING: the scheduler pays no attention to it, and chirpie_delete_post is what stops a scheduled post going out. A thread, or a fan-out made in one request, is hidden as the one thing it was made as, so `hidden_ids` in the answer can name more posts than the id you passed.

id.description: Post ID to hide. A thread or fan-out moves whole.

tools.name: chirpie_unhide_post
tools.description: Put a hidden post back in the user's Chirpie listings. The exact undo of chirpie_hide_post, and as with hide, nothing reaches the platform. Unhiding a post that was never hidden succeeds and changes nothing. chirpie_list_posts with include_hidden true lists the hidden posts.

id.description: Post ID to show again. A thread or fan-out moves whole.

tools.name: chirpie_list_accounts
tools.description: List connected social accounts (X/Twitter, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Threads, Mastodon, Instagram, Facebook and Telegram), with `accounts_limit` (how many the plan allows to be active) and `accounts_active` (how many are) beside them, which say whether there is room to connect another. Accounts with `is_active: false` are connected but not publishing; `inactive_reason` says why: `"plan_limit"` means the account was connected while the plan's account limit was already full and can be switched on with chirpie_activate_account, while `"token_revoked"`, `"token_expired"` and `"reauth_required"` mean the platform stopped accepting the stored credential, so the account has to be connected again and anything it had scheduled was cancelled with its quota returned. Retrying a post does not bring an inactive account back: `inactive_reason` says whether chirpie_activate_account or a fresh connect does. An account switched off deliberately carries no reason at all, and chirpie_activate_account switches it back on. Reconnecting an account already held never needs a free slot. `scheduled_posts` is how many scheduled posts are queued against the account, all of which chirpie_deactivate_account would cancel. On LinkedIn, `account_type` says whether the account is the member's own profile (`"member"`) or a LinkedIn Page they administer (`"organization"`); both post the same way, with their own `id`.

tools.name: chirpie_activate_account
tools.description: Activate a connected account so it can publish. Use for accounts listed with `is_active: false`, for example extra Facebook Pages imported beyond the plan's account limit. Fails with a plan-limit error if no slot is free; deactivating another account frees one.

tools.name: chirpie_deactivate_account
tools.description: Deactivate a connected account. It stops publishing and frees a slot against the plan's account limit, but stays connected so it can be activated again without reauthorizing. CANCELS the account's scheduled posts: a deactivated account cannot publish, so every post queued against it is cancelled and its monthly quota returned, and `canceled_posts` in the response says how many. Activating the account again does NOT restore them. `scheduled_posts` in chirpie_list_accounts says beforehand how many posts this would cancel.

tools.name: chirpie_disconnect_account
tools.description: Disconnect a connected account. The connection is REMOVED: the account stops publishing straight away, frees a slot against the plan's account limit, disappears from chirpie_list_accounts, and calling this again with the same id answers 404. Reconnecting it means the user authorizing Chirpie on that platform again, whereas chirpie_deactivate_account keeps the connection so the account can come back later without reauthorizing. CANCELS the account's scheduled posts: every post queued against it is cancelled and its monthly quota returned, and `canceled_posts` in the response says how many. They are NOT restored. Posts the account already published keep their history, but stop reporting its handle and come back with `account_id: null`. `scheduled_posts` in chirpie_list_accounts says beforehand how many posts this would cancel. Cannot be undone.

tools.name: chirpie_analytics
tools.description: Get analytics (likes, reposts, replies, etc.) for a published post on X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Threads, Mastodon, Instagram or Facebook. Note: Telegram does not expose analytics. The numbers come from a stored snapshot that is at most an hour old, so calling this often costs nothing; set refresh to ask the platform now instead.

post_id.description: Post ID to get analytics for

refresh.description: Ask the platform for the current numbers instead of reading the stored snapshot. Allowed once per post every 5 minutes; past that it answers 429 analytics_refresh_rate_limited with a Retry-After, and the stored numbers are still one ordinary call away.

tools.name: chirpie_list_comments
tools.description: List the comments on a post you published, newest first. Answers from Chirpie's stored snapshot, which is refreshed on a schedule, so the response carries a `sync` object saying how fresh it is (anything but status `ok` has a ready-worded sentence in `sync.reason`) and a `capabilities` object saying what this platform allows: `reply`, `hide`, `delete_own` and `delete_any`. `delete_any` says whether somebody else's comment can be deleted. Page with `next_cursor`. Listing costs nothing, but replying publishes a post and so uses one post from the monthly quota.

post_id.description: Post ID whose comments to list

cursor.description: The next_cursor from the previous page

since.description: ISO 8601 datetime: only comments posted after it

sync.description: 'auto' (default) refreshes when the platform's refresh window has passed, 'true' asks for a refresh now (honoured a minute after the last refresh, 15 minutes on X; sync.next_sync_after says when), 'false' reads what is stored without one

include_hidden.description: Include comments you have hidden (they carry hidden: true)

include_deleted.description: Include deleted comments (they carry deleted: true and keep the last text Chirpie stored). Deleting a comment on Facebook, Instagram, Threads or LinkedIn deletes its replies too

tools.name: chirpie_reply_to_comment
tools.description: Reply to a comment on a post you published. The reply is published to the platform like any other post, so it counts as one post against the monthly quota, and an X reply whose text contains a link is billed at $0.25 on paid plans and rejected on the Free plan. The same per-platform character limits as a post apply.

post_id.description: Post ID the comment is on

idempotency_key.description: A key of your own making that makes retrying this call safe. The same key with the same request replays the first answer for 24 hours instead of sending it again; the same key with a different request is refused with 422 idempotency_key_reused, and a retry that arrives while the first is still running is refused with 409 idempotency_in_progress; a retry after the first has finished collects the replay.

tools.name: chirpie_hide_comment
tools.description: Hide or unhide a comment on a post you published. Facebook, Instagram and Threads support hiding; everywhere else this reports comment_action_unsupported rather than reporting success for something that did not happen. A hidden comment stays in Chirpie's listing behind include_hidden, so the moderation history is kept.

post_id.description: Post ID the comment is on

hidden.description: true (default) hides the comment, false shows it again

tools.name: chirpie_delete_comment
tools.description: Delete a comment on a post you published. It is deleted from the platform first and recorded as deleted in Chirpie only once that succeeded, so a comment is never reported gone while it is still public. On Facebook, Instagram, Threads and LinkedIn the platform deletes the replies under it too, and Chirpie records them deleted as well. Most platforms allow deleting only replies the account wrote; capabilities.delete_any from chirpie_list_comments says whether this one allows deleting somebody else's comment. A deleted comment cannot be restored.

post_id.description: Post ID the comment is on

tools.name: chirpie_create_key
tools.description: Create a new Chirpie API key. Returns the full key once: keys are prefixed `chirpie_sk_` and the API never shows one again. Named scopes give a key that can do less than the calling key: a key created without any can do everything the key that made it can, and a key can never grant a scope it does not itself hold.

scopes.description: What the new key may do. Leave it out for a key that can do exactly what the calling key can do. Reading and listing API keys needs keys:write, because the key list is the inventory of the account's credentials.

tools.name: chirpie_list_keys
tools.description: List the user's Chirpie API keys (prefix + metadata; the full key is only shown on creation).

tools.name: chirpie_revoke_key
tools.description: Revoke a Chirpie API key by its ID. Revocation is permanent and immediate.

tools.name: chirpie_connect_x
tools.description: Start the OAuth flow for a X/Twitter account. Returns an authorization_url the user must open in a browser to complete the connection.

tools.name: chirpie_connect_linkedin
tools.description: Start the OAuth flow for a LinkedIn profile account. Returns an authorization_url the user must open in a browser to complete the connection.

tools.name: chirpie_connect_threads
tools.description: Start the OAuth flow for a Threads account. Returns an authorization_url the user must open in a browser to complete the connection. Coming soon.

tools.name: chirpie_connect_facebook
tools.description: Start the OAuth flow for a Facebook Pages account. Returns an authorization_url the user must open in a browser to complete the connection. Coming soon.

tools.name: chirpie_connect_instagram
tools.description: Start the OAuth flow for an Instagram account. Returns an authorization_url the user must open in a browser to complete the connection. There are two routes and they differ in what the account can do afterwards: `instagram` signs in with Instagram and needs no Facebook Page, while `facebook` signs in with Facebook, connects the Instagram professional accounts linked to the Pages the user shares, and is the only route where chirpie_delete_post can remove a published Instagram post. One Facebook grant can connect several accounts at once; any beyond the plan's account limit are stored switched off rather than dropped. Coming soon.

via.description: Which route to use. 'instagram' (the default) needs no Facebook Page. 'facebook' requires the Instagram professional account to be linked to a Facebook Page, and is the only route where a published post can be deleted.

reconnect.description: Set when the user has been through this consent screen before, so anything they turned down last time is asked again.

tools.name: chirpie_connect_bluesky
tools.description: Connect a Bluesky account using an app password (create one at https://bsky.app/settings/app-passwords).

identifier.description: Bluesky handle. The first part alone is enough ("user"), and "user.bsky.social", a handle on your own domain, or the account email also work.

tools.name: chirpie_connect_mastodon
tools.description: Start the OAuth flow for a Mastodon account on a specific instance.

instance_url.description: Mastodon instance. A bare host is enough ("mastodon.social"), and "https://mastodon.social" or an "@you@fosstodon.org" address also work.

tools.name: chirpie_connect_telegram
tools.description: Connect a Telegram bot. Create a bot with @BotFather on Telegram, then pass the bot token and the chat ID (user, group, or channel).

chat_id.description: Target chat. A bare channel name is enough ("channelname"), and "@channelname", a t.me link, or a numeric chat ID also work.

tools.name: chirpie_set_x_keys
tools.description: Register the user's OWN X developer app (from developer.x.com) so their X accounts connect through it and post against their X API credits instead of Chirpie's. Link posts from accounts connected this way are not surcharged. After setting keys, the user must add the returned redirect_uri as a callback URI on their X app and then reconnect each X account (chirpie_connect_x) to move it onto their app.

client_secret.description: OAuth 2.0 Client Secret from developer.x.com. Stored encrypted and never returned.

label.description: Optional human-readable name for the app

annotations.title: Set your own X developer app

tools.name: chirpie_get_x_keys_status
tools.description: Check whether the user has registered their own X developer app. Returns configuration status and the callback URI to register on the X app, never the client secret.

annotations.title: Check your own X developer app

tools.name: chirpie_remove_x_keys
tools.description: Remove the user's own X developer app. X accounts connected through it stop refreshing until the keys are re-added or the accounts are reconnected through Chirpie's app.

annotations.title: Remove your own X developer app

instructions:
Chirpie publishes to the user's connected social accounts through one API.
chirpie_list_accounts returns the account_id every post and thread names, and says which accounts are active; an account that is not active cannot publish. Analytics and comments name a post_id, from chirpie_list_posts or the post that was just created.
chirpie_post and chirpie_thread publish now, schedule with schedule_at, or save a draft with draft: true; account_ids publishes to several accounts in one call.
chirpie_upload_media returns the id a post, thread or edit attaches media by.
chirpie_list_posts, chirpie_get_post, chirpie_analytics and chirpie_list_comments only read. Deleting a published post or a comment removes it from the platform and cannot be undone; chirpie_hide_post is the reversible way to keep a post out of the listings.
An error from the API carries a code and a sentence saying what to do next. chirpie_post, chirpie_thread, chirpie_upload_media, chirpie_reply_to_comment and chirpie_retry_first_comment take an idempotency_key that makes retrying them safe; other tools have none.
Docs: https://chirpie.ai/docs/mcp
